title.zh: 卷25 長孫嵩 長孫道生
title.raw: 卷25 長孫嵩 長孫道生 Volume 25: Zhang Sunsong, Zhangsun Daosheng

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩 長孫道生

translations.literal: Changsun Song; Changsun Daosheng
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Changsun Song and Changsun Daosheng

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩，代人也，太祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Changsun Song was a man of Dai; the Founding Emperor bestowed the name on him.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song came from Dai; Taizu gave him the name by which he is known.

sentences.zh: 父仁，昭成時為南部大人。

translations.literal: His father Ren, in Emperor Zhaocheng's reign, was southern grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren had served as southern grandee under Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 嵩寬雅有器度，年十四，代父統軍。

translations.literal: Song was magnanimous and refined and possessed of bearing; at fourteen he took his father's place in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded, graceful, and statesmanlike, Song at fourteen succeeded his father in command of the host.

sentences.zh: 昭成末年，諸部乖亂，苻堅使劉庫仁攝國事，嵩與元他等率部眾歸之。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Zhaocheng the tribes fell into disorder; Fu Jian had Liu Kuren oversee state affairs; Song with Yuan Ta and others led their followers to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaocheng's reign was ending the tribes turned unruly; Fu Jian set Liu Kuren to govern the realm, and Song with Yuan Ta and the rest brought their people in to him.

sentences.zh: 劉顯之謀難也，嵩率舊人及鄉邑七百餘家叛顯走，[2]將至五原。

translations.literal: When Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Song led more than seven hundred households of old followers and native places in deserting Xian and fleeing, [2] intending to reach Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Xian's treason Song broke away with seven hundred-odd households of old retainers and home districts, [2] making for Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 時寔君之子，亦聚眾自立，嵩欲歸之。

translations.literal: At that time Shijun's son also gathered forces and set himself up; Song wished to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun's son had meanwhile mustered men and declared himself leader; Song meant to go over to him.

sentences.zh: 見于烏渥，稱逆父之子，勸嵩歸太祖。

translations.literal: Meeting at Wuwo, he called himself the son of a rebellious father and urged Song to submit to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuwo he met Song, styled himself a son who had turned against his father, and pressed him to submit to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 嵩未決，烏渥回其牛首，嵩僶俛從之。

translations.literal: Song was undecided; Wuwo turned his ox's head about, and Song bowed low and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Song still hesitated until Wuwo swung his ox about on the road; then Song bowed his head and went along.

sentences.zh: 見太祖于三漢亭。

translations.literal: He met Taizu at Sanhan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to Taizu at Sanhan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 太祖承大統，復以為南部大人。

translations.literal: When Taizu assumed the great succession, he again made him southern grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu took the great mandate, he restored Song as southern grandee.

sentences.zh: 累著軍功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly distinguished himself in military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle he piled up honors on the field.

sentences.zh: 後從征中山，除冀州刺史，賜爵鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan, was made inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He later marched against Zhongshan, was named inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、司徒、相州刺史，封南平公，所在著稱。

translations.literal: He served in succession as attendant-in-ordinary, minister over the masses, and inspector of Xiangzhou; was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping and won renown wherever he was posted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through attendant-in-ordinary, minister over the masses, and inspector of Xiangzhou, was made Duke of Nanping, and wherever he served his name was praised.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，與山陽侯奚斤、北新侯安同、白馬侯崔宏等八人，坐止車門右，聽理萬幾，故世號八公。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he with Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin, Marquis of Beixin An Tong, Marquis of Baima Cui Hong, and five others — eight in all — sat to the right of the Halting-Chariot Gate hearing and deciding the myriad affairs of state; hence the age called them the Eight Lords.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he joined Xi Jin, Marquis of Shanyang, An Tong, Marquis of Beixin, Cui Hong, Marquis of Baima, and five others — eight men who sat to the right of the Halting-Chariot Gate to hear and settle the realm's business — and men of the time called them the Eight Lords.

sentences.zh: 晉將劉裕之伐姚泓，太宗假嵩節，督山東諸軍事，傳詣平原，緣河北岸，列軍次於畔城。

translations.literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his tally of authority and made him overseer of all military affairs east of the mountains; he was sent to Pingyuan, marched along the north bank of the Yellow River, and drew up his army at Pancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu of Jin marched against Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his staff and made him overseer of armies east of the mountains; he went to Pingyuan, followed the north bank of the Yellow River, and encamped at Pancheng.

sentences.zh: 軍頗失利。

translations.literal: The army met with considerable setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign went badly in several clashes.

sentences.zh: 詔假裕道，裕於舟中望嵩麾蓋，遺以酃酒及江南食物，嵩皆送京師。

translations.literal: An edict granted Liu Yu passage; from his boat Yu gazed at Song's banners and canopies and sent him wine from Ling and foods of the Jiang region; Song had them all forwarded to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Liu Yu free passage; from his boat Yu looked on Song's banners and sent Ling wine and delicacies of the south — Song forwarded everything to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔嵩厚答之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Song to reply with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Song to return the courtesy in full measure.

sentences.zh: 又敕簡精兵為戰備，若裕西過者，便率精銳南出彭沛，如不時過，但引軍隨之。

translations.literal: He further charged him to select elite troops for war readiness: if Yu passed westward, Song was to lead picked forces south into Peng and Pei; if Yu did not pass in season, he was only to trail the army with his own.
translations.idiomatic: He also told him to pick crack troops for battle: if Yu crossed west, strike south into Peng and Pei with the elite; if Yu did not pass on schedule, simply follow with the host.

sentences.zh: 彼至崤陝間，必與姚泓相持，一死一傷，眾力疲弊。

translations.literal: When they reached the Xiao-Shan corridor they would surely grapple with Yao Hong — one side dead, one wounded, their strength spent.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the country between Xiao and Shan they would be locked with Yao Hong — one dead, one hurt, both armies spent.

sentences.zh: 比及秋月，徐乃乘之，則裕首可不戰而懸。

translations.literal: Wait until autumn moon, then strike at leisure, and Liu Yu's head might hang without a battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the autumn moon, move at ease, and Liu Yu's head might be taken without a fight.

sentences.zh: 於是叔孫建等尋河趣洛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jian and the rest then followed the river toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遂入關。

translations.literal: They then entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the passes.

sentences.zh: [3]嵩與建等自成皐南濟，晉諸屯戍皆望塵奔潰。

translations.literal: [3] Song with Jian and the rest crossed south from Chenggao; every Jin garrison they met fled at the dust of their approach.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Song and Jian crossed south from Chenggao; Jin outposts everywhere broke and ran at their dust.

sentences.zh: 裕克長安，嵩乃班師。

translations.literal: When Yu took Chang'an, Song withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Yu had Chang'an, Song led the army home.

sentences.zh: 太宗寢疾，問後事於嵩，嵩曰：「立長則順，以德則人服。

translations.literal: Taizong lay ill in bed and asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To establish the eldest is accordance with order; to establish by virtue is to win men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, bedridden, asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To set up the eldest is to follow order; to set up by virtue is to win hearts.

sentences.zh: 今長皇子賢而世嫡，天所命也，請立。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son is worthy and the hereditary heir — Heaven's mandate; I beg that he be established.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest imperial son is able and the rightful heir — Heaven has chosen him; I beg that he be established.

sentences.zh: 」乃定策禁中。

translations.literal: " Thus the decision was fixed within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: " With that the choice was settled inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 於是詔世祖臨朝監國，嵩為左輔。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict had Shizu attend court and oversee the state; Song was made left supporter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then had Shizu preside at court and oversee the realm; Song was made left supporter.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進爵北平王，司州中正。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession Song was raised to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.

sentences.zh: 詔問公卿，赫連、蠕蠕征討何先。

translations.literal: An edict asked the ministers whether to campaign first against the Helian or the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the ministers whether the Helian or the Rouran should be attacked first.

sentences.zh: 嵩與平陽王長孫翰、司空奚斤等曰：「赫連居土，未能為患，蠕蠕世為邊害，宜先討大檀。

translations.literal: Song with Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han, Minister of Works Xi Jin, and others said: "The Helian hold to their soil and cannot yet be a grave threat; the Rouran have for generations been a frontier scourge — it is right to strike Dadan first.
translations.idiomatic: Song with Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, Xi Jin, Minister of Works, and the rest said: "The Helian cling to their land and are not yet a great peril; the Rouran have long harried the border — strike Dadan first.

sentences.zh: 及則收其畜產，足以富國；

translations.literal: If we reach them in time and seize their herds, that alone will enrich the state;
translations.idiomatic: Catch them in time and take their livestock and the realm grows rich;

sentences.zh: 不及則校獵陰山，多殺禽獸，皮肉筋角，以充軍實，亦愈於破一小國。

translations.literal: if we do not reach them, hunt the Yin Mountains, slaughter beasts in number, and fill the army's stores with hide, flesh, sinew, and horn — that too is better than crushing a petty state.
translations.idiomatic: if not, hunt the Yin Mountains, kill game in masses, and stock the host with hide, meat, sinew, and horn — still better than breaking some small kingdom.

sentences.zh: 」太常崔浩曰：「大檀遷徙鳥逝，疾追則不足經久，大眾則不能及之。

translations.literal: " Grand Minister of Ceremonials Cui Hao said: "Dadan shifts like birds in flight; a swift pursuit cannot be sustained, and a great host cannot overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Hao, Grand Minister of Ceremonials, said: "Dadan vanishes like migrating birds — hot pursuit cannot last, and a great army cannot catch him.

sentences.zh: 赫連屈丐，土宇不過千里，其刑政殘虐，人神所棄，宜先討之。

translations.literal: Helian Qugai's domain is no more than a thousand li; his punishments and government are cruel — abandoned by men and spirits alike; he should be attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Qugai holds barely a thousand li; his laws are savage and men and gods alike have turned from him — attack him first.

sentences.zh: 」尚書劉潔、武京侯安原請先平馮跋。

translations.literal: " Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked to pacify Feng Bo first.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Jie of the Masters of Writing and An Yuan, Marquis of Wujing, urged that Feng Bo be subdued first.

sentences.zh: [4]帝默然，遂西巡狩。

translations.literal: [4] The Emperor was silent and thereafter went west on tour.
translations.idiomatic: [4] The Emperor said nothing and went west on a hunting tour.

sentences.zh: 後聞屈丐死，關中大亂，議欲征之。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that Qugai had died and that Guanzhong was in great disorder, the court debated an expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Later word came that Qugai was dead and Guanzhong in turmoil; the court debated marching west.

sentences.zh: 嵩等曰：「彼若城守，以逸代勞，大檀聞之，乘虛而寇，危道也。

translations.literal: Song and the others said: "If they hold the walls and meet our strength with ease, Dadan will hear of it and raid while we are exposed — a perilous road.
translations.idiomatic: Song and the rest said: "If they sit behind walls and trade our strength for their rest, Dadan will hear and strike our flank — a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃問幽微於天師寇謙之，[5]謙之勸行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then asked the subtle signs of Heaven from the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi; [5] Qianzhi urged the march.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then asked the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi for Heaven's hidden signs; [5] Qianzhi urged him to go.

sentences.zh: 杜超之贊成之，[6]崔浩又言西伐利。

translations.literal: Du Chao endorsed it; [6] Cui Hao again spoke of the profit in a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao backed the plan; [6] Cui Hao again argued the gain of a western war.

sentences.zh: 嵩等固諫不可。

translations.literal: Song and the others firmly remonstrated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Song and his party remonstrated hard that the move must not be made.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，責嵩在官貪污，使武士頓辱。

translations.literal: The Emperor was furious, accused Song of corruption in office, and had armored men publicly humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into rage, charged Song with graft in office, and had warriors shame him in public.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 久之，加柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was given the added title Grand General with Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he received the added rank Grand General with Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 自是，輿駕征伐，嵩以元老多留鎮京師，坐朝堂，平斷刑獄。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, Song as an elder statesman mostly remained to guard the capital, sitting in the hall of court and judging criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the Emperor marched out, Song — by then the senior man of the court — usually stayed to hold the capital, presiding in the hall of court to settle suits at law.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away at eighty.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後高祖追錄先朝功臣，以嵩配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu, recalling the merit of the former court, had Song enshrined to share sacrifice in the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozu, honoring the founders, had Song given a place in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子頹，善騎射，彎弓三百斤。

translations.literal: His son Tui was skilled at mounted archery and could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tui excelled in horsemanship and archery and bent a three-hundred-jin bow.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank and was made attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, was made attendant-in-ordinary, and named General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 有罪，黜為戍兵，後復爵。

translations.literal: For an offense he was reduced to garrison soldier; later his noble rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of a crime, he was demoted to frontier garrison duty; his noble rank was later restored.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰安王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title King An.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled King An.

sentences.zh: 子敦，字孝友，位北鎮都將。

translations.literal: His son Dun, styled Xiaoyou, held the post of chief general of the northern garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun, whose style was Xiaoyou, served as chief general of the northern garrison.

sentences.zh: 坐黷貨，降為公。

translations.literal: For venality he was demoted to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Graft in office cost him his princely rank; he was made a duke.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，自頌先世勳重，[7]復其王爵。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's reign he himself praised the weight of his forebears' service; [7] his kingly rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he himself recited the heavy merit of his line; [7] his royal title was restored.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡簡王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title King Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled King Jian.

sentences.zh: 子道，字念僧，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 久之，隨例降為公，位右衞將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while, by the usual rule he was demoted to duke and held the post of General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In time, under the usual demotion, he became a duke and served as General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡慎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Shen.

sentences.zh: 子悅，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yue inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 建義初，復本王爵，尋降為公。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Jianyi era his original kingly rank was restored; soon he was again demoted to duke.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyi his royal title was restored; before long he was reduced again to duke.

sentences.zh: 位光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 長孫道生，嵩從子也。

translations.literal: Changsun Daosheng was Song's cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Daosheng was Song's nephew.

sentences.zh: 忠厚廉謹，太祖愛其慎重，使掌幾密，與賀毗等四人內侍左右，出入詔命。

translations.literal: Steadfast, loyal, and scrupulous, Taizu loved his careful manner and put him in charge of confidential affairs; with He Pi and three others he attended within at the left and right, bearing edicts in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast, loyal, and careful, he won Taizu's trust for his gravity; Taizu set him over secret matters, and with He Pi and three others he waited on the throne, carrying orders in and out.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，除南統將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was made General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was named General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 後取人美女以獻太宗，切責之，以舊臣不加罪黜。

translations.literal: Later he took a beautiful woman and presented her to Taizong; Taizong sternly rebuked him but, as an old servant, did not punish or dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took a beautiful woman and offered her to Taizong; Taizong rebuked him sharply yet, as a veteran of the founding, withheld punishment or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進爵汝陰公，[8]遷廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he was raised to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was moved to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，與尉眷等率眾出白黑兩漠間，大捷而還。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led forces out between the White and Black Deserts and returned in great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led troops through the country between the White and Black Deserts and came back in triumph.

sentences.zh: 世祖征赫連昌，道生與司徒長孫翰、宗正娥青為前驅，遂平其國。

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Minister of Works Changsun Han and Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing served as vanguard and thereupon pacified the state.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Changsun Han, Minister of Works, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led the van and brought the realm down.

sentences.zh: 昌弟定走保平涼，劉義隆遣將到彥之、王仲德寇河南以救定。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Ding fled to hold Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent the generals Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to raid Henan and rescue Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Ding withdrew to Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to strike Henan and relieve Ding.

sentences.zh: 詔道生與丹陽王太之屯河上以禦之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Daosheng with Prince of Danyang Taizhi to encamp on the river and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Daosheng and Taizhi, Prince of Danyang, to hold the river line against them.

sentences.zh: 遂誘義隆將檀道濟，邀其前後，追至歷城而還。

translations.literal: They thereupon lured Liu Yilong's general Tan Daoji, caught him between front and rear, pursued him to Licheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They baited Tan Daoji of Liu Yilong's host, caught him fore and aft, chased him to Licheng, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 除司空，加侍中，進封上黨王。

translations.literal: He was made Minister of Works, added attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced to Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Minister of Works and attendant-in-ordinary and raised to Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 道生廉約，身為三司，而衣不華飾，食不兼味。

translations.literal: Daosheng was frugal; though he held one of the Three Excellencies, his clothes bore no rich ornament and his meals no second dish.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng lived sparely: though a pillar of state, he wore no finery and ate but one course.

sentences.zh: 一熊皮鄣泥，數十年不易，時人比之晏嬰。

translations.literal: A single bear-pelt mud-guard he did not change for decades; men of the time compared him to Yan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: One bear-hide riding apron he kept for decades without replacing; his contemporaries likened him to Yan Ying.

sentences.zh: 第宅卑陋，出鎮後，其子弟頗更修繕，起堂廡。

translations.literal: His house was low and mean; after he went out on garrison duty his sons and nephews somewhat repaired it and raised halls and galleries.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling was humble; once he had left on frontier command his sons and nephews refurbished it and built halls.

sentences.zh: 道生還，歎曰：「昔霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，今強寇尚遊魂漠北，吾豈可安坐華美也！

translations.literal: When Daosheng returned he sighed and said: "In old times Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed he would not concern himself with a household — and now strong foes still wander the soul of the northern desert; how can I sit at ease amid splendor!
translations.idiomatic: On his return Daosheng sighed: "Huo Qubing once said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed a man had no business with a home — and mighty enemies still haunt the northern sands; how should I dwell in comfort and show?

sentences.zh: 」乃切責子弟，令毀宅。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sternly rebuked his sons and nephews and ordered the house destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " He rebuked his sons and nephews harshly and made them tear the house down.

sentences.zh: 其恭慎如此。

translations.literal: Such was his respectful caution.
translations.idiomatic: In such ways he kept his reverent care.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，所在著績，每建大議，多合時機。

translations.literal: In Shizu's age he won distinction wherever he served; whenever he framed a great proposal it mostly matched the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu he left his mark in every post; on great questions his counsel usually hit the hour.

sentences.zh: 為將有權略，善待士眾。

translations.literal: As a general he had stratagem and treated officers and men well.
translations.idiomatic: In command he was resourceful and kind to his troops.

sentences.zh: 帝命歌工歷頌羣臣，曰：「智如崔浩，廉如道生。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered singing masters to go through the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, frugal as Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had singers pass among the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, spare as Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 」及年老，頗惑其妻孟氏，以此見譏。

translations.literal: " In his old age he was much swayed by his wife Lady Meng, for which he was mocked.
translations.idiomatic: " In age he fell under his wife Lady Meng's sway and was laughed at for it.

sentences.zh: 與從父嵩俱為三公，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: He and his uncle Song both held one of the Three Excellencies — an honor for their generation.
translations.idiomatic: He and his uncle Song both reached the Three Excellencies — a glory of their day.

sentences.zh: 子抗，[9]位少卿，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Kang, [9] held the post of Vice Director; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang, [9] served as Vice Director and died young.

sentences.zh: 抗子觀，少以壯勇知名，後襲祖爵上黨王。

translations.literal: Kang's son Guan, in youth famed for bold courage, later inherited his grandfather's rank as Prince of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Guan won early fame for fierce courage and later inherited his grandfather's title as Prince of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時異姓諸王，襲爵多降為公，帝以其祖道生佐命先朝，故特不降。

translations.literal: At that time most kings of other surnames who inherited were demoted to duke; because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding court, the Emperor specially did not lower his rank.
translations.idiomatic: By then most non-imperial clansmen who inherited were cut to duke; because Daosheng had served the founding, the Emperor left Guan's princely rank untouched.

sentences.zh: 以征西大將軍、假司空、督河西七鎮諸軍，討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven garrisons of the Hexi circuit, to campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven Hexi garrisons to strike Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 部帥拾寅遁藏，焚其所居城邑而還。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Shiyin fled into hiding; Guan burned his towns and strongholds and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun chief Shiyin vanished into concealment; Guan burned his settlements and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，拜殿中尚書、侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾又侵逼，復假觀司空討降之。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun again pressed the border, Guan was again lent the acting rank of Minister of Works to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided again, Guan was again lent the acting seal of Minister of Works to bring them to heel.

sentences.zh: 後為征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 葬禮依其祖靖王故事，陪葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: His funeral followed the precedent of his grandfather King Jing and he was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His burial followed his grandfather King Jing's rites, and he was laid to rest beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 子冀歸，六歲襲爵，降為公。

translations.literal: Ziji returned; at age six he inherited the title, which was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziji came home, his son at six inherited the rank, lowered to duke.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其幼承家業，賜名稚，字承業。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he succeeded the family estate while young, bestowed the name Zhi, style Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing him take up the house while still a boy, gave him the name Zhi, styled Chengye.

sentences.zh: 稚聰敏有才藝，虛心愛士。

translations.literal: Zhi was clever and talented, modest and fond of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was quick-witted and skilled, humble, and devoted to men of talent.

sentences.zh: 為前將軍，從高祖南討，授七兵尚書、太常卿、右將軍。

translations.literal: As Forward General he followed Gaozu on the southern campaign and was appointed Minister of the Seven Arms, Grand Minister of Ceremonies, and Right General.
translations.idiomatic: As forward general he followed Gaozu south and received the posts of minister of the seven arms, grand minister of ceremonies, and right general.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，侯剛子淵，稚之女壻。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time Hou Gang's son Yuan married Zhi's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, Hou Gang's son Yuan became Zhi's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 剛為元叉所厚，故稚驟得轉進。

translations.literal: Gang was favored by Yuan Cha, and so Zhi was repeatedly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Gang stood high with Yuan Cha, and Zhi rose in rank again and again.

sentences.zh: 出為撫軍大將軍，領揚州刺史，假鎮南大將軍，都督淮南諸軍事。

translations.literal: He went out as Pacification Army Grand General, acting Inspector of Yangzhou, with acting title General Who Pacifies the South and command over all military affairs in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as pacification-army grand general and inspector of Yangzhou, with acting rank as general who pacifies the south and command of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍將裴邃、虞鴻襲據壽春，稚諸子驍果，邃頗難之，號曰「鐵小兒」。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's generals Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized the outer wall of Shouchun; Zhi's sons were fierce fighters, and Sui found them hard to face, calling them the "little men of iron."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui and Yu Hong of Liang seized Shouchun's outer ramparts; Zhi's sons fought like iron, and Sui, finding them hard to beat, called them the "iron boys."

sentences.zh: 詔河間王琛總眾援之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Hejian Chen to take overall command and reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Prince of Hejian Chen in overall command to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 琛欲決戰，稚以雨久，更須持重。

translations.literal: Chen wished to give battle; Zhi, because the rains had lasted long, said they must still be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Chen wanted a pitched battle; Zhi, with the rains dragging on, urged restraint.

sentences.zh: 琛弗從，遂戰，為賊所乘，稚後殿。

translations.literal: Chen would not follow; they fought and the enemy took advantage; Zhi brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Chen refused; the enemy turned the fight, and Zhi covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 初，稚既總強兵，久不決戰，議者疑有異圖。

translations.literal: At first, because Zhi held strong forces yet would not decide battle for a long time, critics suspected ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: At first, with strong troops under him and no battle for a long while, some suspected another design.

sentences.zh: 朝廷重遣河間王琛及臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等三都督外聲助稚，內實防之。

translations.literal: The court again sent Prince of Hejian Chen, Prince of Linhuai Yu, and Minister of Writing Li Xian as three area commanders—outwardly to aid Zhi, inwardly in fact to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Chen of Hejian, Yu of Linhuai, and Li Xian of the Masters of Writing as three commanders—nominally to help Zhi, in truth to watch him.

sentences.zh: 會鮮于脩禮反於中山，以稚為大都督北討。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Zhongshan, Zhi was made Grand Commander for the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianyu Xiuli rose at Zhongshan, Zhi was made grand commander of the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 尋以本使達鄴城。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, in his capacity as envoy he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, still acting as envoy, he reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔稚解行臺，罷大使，遣河間王琛為大都督，酈道元為行臺。

translations.literal: An edict relieved Zhi of the mobile secretariat and dismissed him as grand envoy; Prince of Hejian Chen was made Grand Commander and Li Daoyuan mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Zhi of the mobile secretariat and envoy's powers; Chen of Hejian became grand commander and Li Daoyuan mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稚遣子子裕奉表，稱與琛同在淮南，俱當國難，琛敗臣全，遂生私隙。

translations.literal: Zhi sent his son Ziyu with a memorial stating that he and Chen were together in Huainan, both facing the state's peril; Chen was defeated while he held the line, and private rancor arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent his son Ziyu with a memorial: he and Chen had shared Huainan in national crisis; Chen lost while he held firm, and private bitterness followed.

sentences.zh: 且臨機奪帥，非算所長。

translations.literal: Moreover, seizing command on the spot was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, snatching command in the field was not his gift.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 琛與稚前到呼沱，稚未欲戰，而琛不從。

translations.literal: Chen and Zhi went on ahead to Hutuo; Zhi did not yet wish to fight, but Chen would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Zhi reached Hutuo; Zhi still held back from battle, and Chen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 行達五鹿，為脩禮邀擊，琛不赴之。

translations.literal: On the march they reached Wulu; Xiuli intercepted them, and Chen did not go to the fight.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulu, Xiuli ambushed them; Chen would not engage.

sentences.zh: 賊總至，遂大敗，稚與琛並除名。

translations.literal: When the rebels massed, they were utterly defeated; Zhi and Chen were both struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gathered and routed them; Zhi and Chen were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋而正平郡蜀反，復假稚鎮西將軍、討蜀都督，頻戰有功，除平東將軍，復本爵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Shu rebelled in Zhengping commandery; Zhi was again given acting title General Who Pacifies the West and Commander to Suppress Shu, fought repeatedly with merit, was made General Who Pacifies the East, and restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shu soon rebelled in Zhengping; Zhi was again made acting general who pacifies the west and commander against Shu, won repeated victories, was made general who pacifies the east, and restored to his old title.

sentences.zh: 後除尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He later became right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，復以稚為行臺討之。

translations.literal: Before long, Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Baoyin held the province in rebellion; Zhi was again made mobile secretariat to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Baoyin rebelled as inspector of Yongzhou; Zhi was again sent as mobile secretariat to crush him.

sentences.zh: 稚時背疽未愈，靈太后勞之曰：「卿疹源如此，朕欲相停，更無可寄如何？

translations.literal: Zhi's back carbuncle had not yet healed; Empress Dowager Ling comforted him, saying: "Your ailment runs so deep; I wished to spare you, yet whom else can I rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's back abscess was still unhealed; Empress Dowager Ling comforted him: "Your sore runs so deep; I would have spared you—yet whom else can I trust?"

sentences.zh: 」稚答曰：「死而後已，敢不自力。

translations.literal: " Zhi answered: "After death one still serves; how dare I not exert myself?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered, "One serves to the grave; how dare I hold back?"

sentences.zh: 」時子彥亦患脚痺，扶杖入辭。

translations.literal: " At that time his son Ziyan also suffered crippling foot ailment and, leaning on a staff, came to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyan, lame in both feet, came on a staff to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射元順顧相謂曰：「吾等備位大臣，各居寵位，危難之日，病者先行，無乃不可乎？

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shun looked at his colleagues and said: "We fill the posts of great ministers, each in favor; on a day of peril, the sick go first—is that not wrong?
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Yuan Shun glanced at his peers and said, "We hold great offices in favor; on a day of danger the sick march first—is that fitting?"

sentences.zh: 」莫有對者。

translations.literal: " No one replied.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 時薛鳳賢反於正平，薛脩義屯聚河東，分據鹽池，攻圍蒲坂，東西連結，以應寶夤。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Fengxian rebelled at Zhengping and Xue Xiuyi gathered forces at Hedong, seized the salt pools, besieged Puban, and east and west linked up in support of Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengxian rebelled at Zhengping; Xue Xiuyi massed at Hedong, held the salt pools, besieged Puban, and linked east and west to Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 稚乃據河東。

translations.literal: Zhi then held Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then secured Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時有詔廢鹽池稅，稚上表曰：「鹽池天資賄貨，密邇京畿，唯須寶而護之，均贍以理。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict abolishing the salt-pool tax; Zhi submitted a memorial stating: "The salt pools are Heaven's gift of wealth, close to the capital region; they must be treasured and guarded and shared out with fair rule.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the salt-pool levy; Zhi memorialized: "The pools are Heaven's wealth at the capital's door; they must be guarded and rationed fairly.

sentences.zh: 今四境多虞，府藏罄竭。

translations.literal: Now on four sides there are many alarms and the treasury is empty.
translations.idiomatic: The borders are alarmed and the treasury bare.

sentences.zh: 然冀定二州且亡且亂，常調之絹，不復可收。

translations.literal: Yet the regular silk levies of Ji and Ding provinces are dying in disorder and can no longer be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Ding are half lost; their regular silk dues cannot be gathered.

sentences.zh: 仰惟府庫，有出無入，必須經綸，出入相補。

translations.literal: Looking to the storehouses, outflow without inflow—there must be planning so expenditure and income balance.
translations.idiomatic: The coffers spend without filling; income and outlay must be balanced.

sentences.zh: 略論鹽稅，一年之中，準絹而言，猶不應減三十萬匹也，便是移冀定二州置於畿甸。

translations.literal: Roughly reckoning the salt tax for one year against silk, it should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts—this is like setting Ji and Ding within the capital belt.
translations.idiomatic: The salt tax alone, reckoned in silk for a year, should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts—like moving Ji and Ding into the inner commanderies.

sentences.zh: 今若廢之，事同再失。

translations.literal: If it is now abolished, the matter is like losing twice.
translations.idiomatic: To abolish it now is to lose twice over.

sentences.zh: 臣前仰違嚴旨，不先討關賊而解河東者，非是閑長安而急蒲坂。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier disobeyed the stern order and did not first attack the border rebels but relieved Hedong—not because he was idle about Chang'an and urgent only for Puban.
translations.idiomatic: I earlier defied your stern order and relieved Hedong before striking the border rebels—not because I slighted Chang'an for Puban.

sentences.zh: 蒲坂一陷，沒失鹽池，三軍口命，濟贍理絕。

translations.literal: Once Puban fell, the salt pools would be lost and the army's mouth would be cut off—relief and supply would end.
translations.idiomatic: Had Puban fallen, the pools would be gone, the army's ration cut, and supply ended.

sentences.zh: 天助大魏，茲計不爽。

translations.literal: Heaven aided Great Wei; this plan did not miss.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aided Great Wei; the plan held.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖昇平之年，無所乏少，猶創置鹽官而加典護，非為物而競利，恐由利而亂俗也。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's years of rising peace there was no want, yet he still created salt officials and added custodians—not for goods and profit, but fearing that profit would corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Gaozu's peaceful years, without want, he set salt officers and overseers—not for profit but lest profit corrupt custom.

sentences.zh: 況今王公素餐，百官尸祿，租徵六年之粟，調折來歲之資，此皆出人私財，奪人膂力。

translations.literal: How much more now, when princes and dukes eat salary without work and officials hold posts without labor, rent taking six years' grain and levies folding next year's funds—these all come from private purses and seize men's strength.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when nobles feast on salary and officials on empty posts, rent taking six years' grain and levies folding next year's funds—all from private purses, all seizing men's strength.

sentences.zh: 豈是願言，事不獲已。

translations.literal: It is not what I wish to say; the matter cannot be helped.
translations.idiomatic: This is not what I wish to say; the matter cannot be helped.

sentences.zh: 臣輒符司監將尉還率所部，依常收稅，更聽後敕。」

translations.literal: Your subject has already ordered the supervising office and commanders to lead their units and collect tax as usual, awaiting further edict."
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered the supervising office and commanders to collect the tax as usual, pending further command."

sentences.zh: 稚克寶夤將侯終德，寶夤出走，雍州平。

translations.literal: Zhi defeated Baoyin's general Hou Zhongde; Baoyin fled and Yongzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi routed Hou Zhongde, Baoyin's general; Baoyin fled and Yongzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 除雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封上黨王，尋改馮翊王，後降為郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang, soon changed to Prince of Fengyi, then reduced to commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangdi's accession he was enfeoffed as prince of Shangdang, soon made prince of Fengyi, then reduced to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，加侍中，兼尚書令、大行臺，仍鎮長安。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, added Palace Attendant, and concurrently Minister of Writing and Grand Mobile Secretariat, still garrisoning Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Masters of Writing, palace attendant, and concurrently minister of writing and grand mobile secretariat, still holding Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝立，遷太尉公，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor was enthroned he was transferred to Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne he was made grand marshal and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之敗，斛斯椿先據河橋，謀誅尒朱。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Hanling, Husi Chun first seized Heqiao and plotted to kill the Erzhu.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanling, Husi Chun seized Heqiao first and plotted to kill the Erzhu.

sentences.zh: 使稚入洛，啟帝誅世隆兄弟之意。

translations.literal: He sent Zhi into Luoyang to inform the emperor of the intent to execute Shilong and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhi into Luoyang to tell the emperor of the plan to kill Shilong and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，轉太傅，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Emperor Who Fled the Capital he was transferred to Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the fleeing emperor's accession he was made grand tutor and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，更封開國子。

translations.literal: For merit in settling the succession he was further enfeoffed as Viscount Who Establishes the State.
translations.idiomatic: For settling the succession he was further enfeoffed as viscount who establishes the state.

sentences.zh: 稚表請回授其姨兄廷尉卿元洪超次子惲。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized asking to transfer the enfeoffment to his maternal cousin's son, Grand Minister of Justice Yuan Hongchao's second son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked to pass the title to his cousin on his mother's side, Grand Minister of Justice Yuan Hongchao's second son Yun.

sentences.zh: 初，稚生而母亡，為洪超母所撫養，是以求讓，許之。

translations.literal: At first Zhi's mother had died when he was born; Hongchao's mother raised him, and for that reason he sought to yield; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had died at his birth; Hongchao's mother raised him, and on that ground his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 出帝入關，稚時鎮虎牢，亦隨赴長安。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Who Fled the Capital entered the passes, Zhi was then garrisoning Hulao and followed to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleeing emperor entered the passes, Zhi was at Hulao and followed him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 稚妻張氏，生二子，子彥、子裕。

translations.literal: Zhi's wife was the Zhang clan; she bore two sons, Ziyan and Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's wife was Lady Zhang; she bore Ziyan and Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 後與羅氏私通，遂殺其夫，棄張納羅。

translations.literal: Later he had an affair with Lady Luo, killed her husband, abandoned Zhang and took Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took Lady Luo in secret, killed her husband, cast off Zhang, and married Luo.

sentences.zh: 羅年大稚十餘歲，妒忌防限。

translations.literal: Luo was more than ten years older than Zhi and jealous and restrictive.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was more than ten years his senior, jealous and controlling.

sentences.zh: 稚雅相愛敬，旁無姻妾，[10]僮侍之中，嫌疑致死者，乃有數四。

translations.literal: Zhi in his grace loved and respected her; beside him there were no consorts or concubines; [10] among male and female attendants, those who died on suspicion of impropriety numbered several.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi adored her and kept no other wives; [10] among servants, several died on mere suspicion.

sentences.zh: 羅生三子，紹遠、士亮、季亮，兄弟皆廉武。

translations.literal: Luo bore three sons, Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang; the brothers were all upright and martial.
translations.idiomatic: Luo bore Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang—brothers all upright and warlike.

sentences.zh: 稚少輕俠，鬬鷄走馬，力爭殺人，因亡抵龍門將陳興德家，會赦乃免。

translations.literal: Zhi in youth was light and chivalrous, cockfighting and racing horses, striving and killing men; he fled for refuge to Longmen General Chen Xingde's house and was spared when an amnesty came.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhi was a swaggerer—cockfights, racing, brawls that killed; he fled to Longmen general Chen Xingde and was spared by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 因以後妻羅前夫女呂氏，妻興德兄興恩以報之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave Luo's former husband's daughter, the Lu clan, in marriage, and married Xingde's elder brother Xingen to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: He then married Luo's stepdaughter of the Lu clan to Xingde's brother Xingen in return.

sentences.zh: 子彥，本名儁，有膂力。

translations.literal: Ziyan, original name Jun, had great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan, born Jun, was immensely strong.

sentences.zh: 以累從父征討功，封槐里縣子。

translations.literal: For repeated merit following his father on campaigns he was enfeoffed Viscount of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: For merit on his father's campaigns he was enfeoffed as viscount of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 出帝與齊獻武王構隙，加子彥中軍大都督、行臺僕射，鎮弘農，以為心膂。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Who Fled the Capital and Duke Xianwu of Qi were at odds, Ziyan was added Central Army Grand Commander and Mobile Secretariat Vice Director, garrisoning Hongnong as a trusted pillar.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleeing emperor and Duke Xianwu of Qi fell out, Ziyan was made central-army grand commander and mobile secretariat vice director at Hongnong as a trusted pillar.

sentences.zh: 後從帝入關。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went with the emperor into the passes.

sentences.zh: 子彥少嘗墜馬折臂，肘上骨起寸餘，乃命開肉鋸骨，流血數升，言戲自若。

translations.literal: Ziyan in youth once fell from a horse and broke his arm; bone stood up more than an inch above the elbow; he ordered the flesh cut open and the bone sawed, blood flowing several sheng, yet he spoke and jested as before.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Ziyan fell and broke his arm; bone jutted an inch above the elbow; he had the flesh opened and the bone sawed, lost pints of blood, and jested through it.

sentences.zh: 時以為踰於關羽。

translations.literal: Men of the time thought it surpassed Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said it surpassed Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 子裕，位衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: Ziyu held the post of Vice Director of the Chamberlain for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was vice director of the chamberlain for the palace.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷二十五 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」。

translations.literal: In the tables of contents of all editions of Wei shu juan 25 this scroll is marked as lacunose.
translations.idiomatic: Every edition's table of contents marks Wei shu juan 25 as lacunose.

sentences.zh: 百衲本、南本、汲本卷末殘存宋人校語：「魏收書列傳第十三。

translations.literal: The Patchwork, Southern, and Jishui editions at the end of the scroll preserve Song-dynasty collation notes: "Wei Shou's book, Biographies section 13.
translations.idiomatic: Patchwork, Southern, and Jishui editions keep Song notes at the scroll's end: "Wei Shou's book, Biographies 13.

sentences.zh: 」局本下補「亡」字。

translations.literal: " The Bureau edition supplies below the character "lost."
translations.idiomatic: " The Bureau edition adds "lost" below.

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書闕，後人所補。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition textual verification states: "Wei Shou's book is lacunose; later men supplemented it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Edition textual notes: "Wei Shou's text is missing; later hands supplied this.

sentences.zh: 」按此卷以北史卷二二長孫嵩、長孫道生傳補，附長孫稚傳有溢出語，當出於高氏小史。

translations.literal: " On examination this scroll was supplemented from Beishi juan 22, the biographies of Changsun Song and Changsun Daosheng; the attached Changsun Zhi biography has overflowing wording that should come from the Gao clan Minor History.
translations.idiomatic: " The received scroll was patched from Beishi juan 22 (Changsuns Song and Daosheng); the attached Zhi life has overflow wording likely from the Gao clan Minor History.

sentences.zh: 嵩率舊人及鄉邑七百餘家叛顯走 北史卷二二長孫嵩傳「鄉邑」作「庶師」。

translations.literal: Song led his old followers and township households, more than seven hundred families, in rebellion and flight. Beishi juan 22, Changsun Song biography, reads "township households" as "subordinate commanders."
translations.idiomatic: "Song led his old followers and township households, more than seven hundred families, in revolt": Beishi juan 22, Song's life, has "township households" as "subordinate commanders."

sentences.zh: 按「庶師」和「舊人」對舉。

translations.literal: Commentary: "subordinate commanders" and "old followers" are set in contrast.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "subordinate commanders" pairs with "old followers."

sentences.zh: 「舊人」指拓跋本部人，「庶師」當是指非本部的諸族人。

translations.literal: "Old followers" means men of the Tuoba core; "subordinate commanders" should mean non-core tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: "Old followers" means core Tuoba men; "subordinate commanders" should mean non-core tribes.

sentences.zh: 疑這裏的「鄉邑」乃後人所改。

translations.literal: It is suspected that here "township households" was altered by later men.
translations.idiomatic: "Township households" here was likely a later change.

sentences.zh: 於是叔孫建等尋河趣洛遂入關 按尋河趣洛者是叔孫建所領魏軍，入關者是劉裕所統的晉軍，這裏牽連敍述，遂似叔孫建等入關。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luo and then entered the passes. Commentary: Those who followed the river toward Luo were the Wei army Shusun Jian led; those who entered the passes were the Jin army Liu Yu commanded—here the narrative is linked, so it seems Shusun Jian and others entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: "Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luo and entered the passes": the river march was Shusun Jian's Wei force; entering the passes was Liu Yu's Jin army—the linked narrative makes it seem Jian entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 疑「遂入關」上脫「裕」字。

translations.literal: It is suspected the character for "Yu" has dropped above "then entered the passes."
translations.idiomatic: Yu (Liu Yu) may have dropped before "entered the passes."

sentences.zh: 尚書劉潔武京侯安原請先平馮跋 卷三０安原傳「武京」作「武原」。

translations.literal: Minister of Writing Liu Jie, Marquis of Wujing, Hou Anyuan, and others asked to pacify Feng Bo first. Juan 30, Anyuan biography, reads "Wujing" as "Wuyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Jie, Marquis of Wujing, Hou Anyuan, and others asked to pacify Feng Bo first: juan 30, Anyuan's life, has "Wujing" as "Wuyuan."

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷一五地理志下徐州彭城國有「武原縣」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Jin shu juan 15, Treatise on Geography, Lower, Xuzhou, Pengcheng commandery, has "Wuyuan county."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Jin shu juan 15, Geography, Lower, Xuzhou, Pengcheng, lists Wuyuan county.

sentences.zh: 地不屬魏，但當時封邑取南朝郡縣名的很多。

translations.literal: The place did not belong to Wei, but at that time many enfeoffments took Southern-dynasty commandery and county names.
translations.idiomatic: It lay outside Wei, yet many fiefs then took Southern-dynasty place-names.

sentences.zh: 「武京」不聞有此縣，此傳「京」字疑誤。

translations.literal: No county of "Wujing" is heard of; the character jing in this biography is suspected to be in error.
translations.idiomatic: No "Wujing" county is known; jing here is likely wrong.

sentences.zh: 帝乃問幽微於天師寇謙之 北史卷二二「微」作「徵」，「微」當是「徵」之訛。

translations.literal: The emperor then asked about hidden and manifest matters of the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi. Beishi juan 22 reads "hidden" as "manifest omen"; "hidden" should be a corruption of "manifest omen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi about hidden and manifest matters: Beishi juan 22 has "hidden" as "manifest omen"; "hidden" corrupts "manifest omen."

sentences.zh: 杜超之贊成之 按杜超，卷八三外戚傳有傳。

translations.literal: Du Chao approved it. Commentary: Du Chao has a biography in juan 83, Outer Kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao approved. Note: Du Chao has a biography in juan 83, Outer Kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 可能是雙名「超之」，單稱作「超」，也可能涉上「寇謙之」而衍「之」字。

translations.literal: It may be the double name "Chaozhi," singly called "Chao," or the character zhi may have been added by contamination from "Kou Qianzhi" above.
translations.idiomatic: This may be the double name Chaozhi, shortened to Chao, or zhi may have crept in from "Kou Qianzhi" above.

sentences.zh: 高宗時自頌先世勳重 諸本「宗」作「祖」。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he himself praised the weight of his forebears' merit. In various editions "zong" is written as "zu."
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he praised his forebears' merit: editions read zong as zu.

sentences.zh: 按事見卷五高宗紀興安二年歲末，「祖」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Commentary: The matter appears in juan 5, Annals of Gaozong, at the end of the second year of Xing'an; "zu" is corrupt and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the event is in juan 5, Gaozong Annals, end of Xing'an year 2; zu is wrong and is corrected.

sentences.zh: 進爵汝陰公 張森楷云：「以前初無封爵之文，而云『進爵』，疑誤。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Ruyin. Zhang Senkai states: "Earlier there was no text of an initial enfeoffment, yet it says 'advanced in rank'—suspected error.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to duke of Ruyin. Zhang Senkai: "No prior enfeoffment is recorded, yet it says 'advanced'—likely error.

sentences.zh: 」按此傳以北史卷二二長孫道生傳補，當是李延壽刪節之失。

translations.literal: " Commentary: This biography was supplemented from Beishi juan 22, Changsun Daosheng biography; it should be Li Yanshou's faulty abridgment.
translations.idiomatic: " This life was patched from Beishi juan 22, Daosheng; the fault is Li Yanshou's abridgment.

sentences.zh: 這種刪節失當，下文還有，如「帝以其祖道生佐命先朝」，不知為何帝；

translations.literal: Such faulty abridgment appears again below—for example, "the emperor, because his grandfather Daosheng aided the founding court," without stating which emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Such cuts recur below—"the emperor, because his grandfather Daosheng aided the founding court," without naming which emperor;

sentences.zh: 「以本使達鄴城」，不知為何使。

translations.literal: "in his capacity as envoy reached Ye," without stating what envoy.
translations.idiomatic: "as envoy reached Ye," without naming the mission.

sentences.zh: 今不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Not all collation notes are given here.
translations.idiomatic: Further collation is not set out in full.

sentences.zh: 子抗 北史卷二二「抗」作「瓬」。

translations.literal: His son Kang: Beishi juan 22 reads "Kang" as "Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang: Beishi juan 22 has Kang as Qiang.

sentences.zh: 旁無姻妾 北史卷二二「姻」作「姬」，是。

translations.literal: Beside him there were no consorts or concubines: Beishi juan 22 reads "consort-clan wives" as "concubines"; that reading is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Beside him there were no consorts or concubines": Beishi juan 22 has "consort-clan wives" as "concubines"; that is correct.
